title: Audit ledgering and residency-aware evidence fabric for admin actions
creator: Avery Chen
description: Build an append-only audit ledger and an evidence export fabric that enforces data residency and retention policies for admin actions, access events, and configuration changes. The feature must provide cryptographic integrity proofs, region-aware WORM (write-once) storage options, automated reporting for compliance audits, and a developer-friendly export interface (JSON/CSV) that filters by residency tags. This ticket scopes design and implementation of the ledger schema, residency tagging, retention enforcement, KMS integration, and the automated evidence/report generation pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions, access grants, and configuration changes are written to an append-only ledger with a tamper-evident hash chain
Each ledger entry includes a residency tag and retention TTL that drives exportability and storage location decisions
Evidence exports for a given tenant and residency region can be produced on-demand and as scheduled reports with signed integrity manifests
Exported artifacts can be stored to a WORM-compatible sink (S3 Object Lock or customer-managed archive) with KMS-managed encryption and key rotation support
End-to-end automated test covering write -> immutable store write -> signed export -> verify integrity succeeds
Documentation and runbook for compliance operations and incident investigators are published
Security review completed and approval attached to the release
implementation_notes: Ledger model: append-only sequence with per-entry SHA-256 hash; entries linked via previous_hash to form a chain. Consider Merkle tree batching for periodic checkpoint signing to reduce signer load.
Residency model: add residency_tag (e.g., eu-west-1, us-east-1) and retention_policy_id to each entry. Enforcement layer routes exports and WORM sinks based on residency_tag.
WORM sinks: support S3 Object Lock governance/compliance modes and a customer-on-prem append-only archive endpoint (signed upload protocol).

KMS: integrate with existing KMS abstraction. Use HSM-backed keys for manifest signing. Support key rotation without losing verifiability by signing new checkpoints and retaining historical public key fingerprints in manifest.

Retention enforcement: background sweeper marks entries tombstoned after retention TTL; tombstones cannot be deleted from WORM sinks but will be excluded from active query results per policy. Retention TTL values are derived from tenant config with min/max guardrails.
Export format: canonical JSONL for record-level exports and compressed CSV for summary exports. Each export includes a signed manifest with timestamp, residency filter, hash root, and signer key ID.
Operational UX: add console endpoint for scheduled evidence exports and ad-hoc forensic queries. Exports produce pre-signed download links with limited expiration and audit trail for access.
Backward compatibility: provide a migration utility to re-ingest key historical events into ledger form for enabled tenants; migration must be run off-peak and have dry-run mode.
progress_updates: 2025-01-16: Kickoff meeting with product, security, and infra. Agreed on residency_tag approach and initial ledger schema fields.
2025-01-22: Prototype of append-only ledger service with in-memory chain and SHA-256 linking. Proof-of-concept for manifest signing completed.
2025-01-30: Design review with Security: HSM-backed signer required for production; added KMS integration workstream. Security requested threat model doc.
2025-02-05: Scoped WORM sink adapters: S3 Object Lock adapter and a stub for on-prem archive. Engineering sprint planned for SDK + sink adapters.
2025-02-12: Implemented residency-aware routing for export requests; unit tests for residency tag validation added.
2025-02-18: First end-to-end demo: write -> ledger append -> sign checkpoint -> export manifest generation. Issues found with concurrency on checkpoint signing; investigating mutex strategies.
review_feedback: PM (Lina Patel): Ensure export retention policy UI surfaces per-tenant legal hold overrides and emergency retention extension flow.
Security (Ravi Gupta): Require HSM-backed signing and an audit of signer key access. Also requested revocation plan for compromised signing keys.
Design (Priya Rao): Console export UX should show residency origin, retention status, and signed-manifest verification status before download.
Infra (Jonas Ek): Recommend using merkle checkpointing every 1M events to avoid per-event signing cost. Also flagged S3 Object Lock region limitations for some customers.
qa_plan: Unit tests for hash-chain integrity and previous_hash linking
Property tests for merkle checkpointing invariants
Integration test writing events to ledger and verifying signed manifest using HSM-backed key simulator
E2E test that runs export pipeline into S3 Object Lock and verifies immutability via object metadata
Run migration dry-run against a snapshot of production events and validate record counts and hashes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): enable ledgering for internal audit tenant and run exports weekly; gather performance metrics
Phase 2 (beta tenants): opt-in for a small set of customers with residency requirements; exercise on-prem sink adapter
Phase 3 (general availability): tenant self-service toggle, console UX enabled, and retention guardrails enforced by defaults
Fallbacks: if checkpoint signer fails, system continues to accept writes but marks checkpoints as unsigned and raises priority alerts; automated retry attempts and manual signer utility available
notes: Trade-offs: per-event signing offers strongest non-repudiation but is costly at scale. Chosen approach uses batched merkle checkpoint signing to balance cost and provability.
Open questions: how to present legal-hold overrides in a way that prevents accidental retention bypass while keeping support workflows manageable?
Next steps: complete HSM integration spike (due 2025-02-28), finalize migration tool prototype, and schedule security review sign-off
